change_summary: Asperger's Disorder was eliminated as a standalone diagnosis and merged into a single Autism Spectrum Disorder category with severity levels.
clinical_rationale: Research showed no reliable clinical distinction between Asperger's, PDD-NOS, and autistic disorder; a spectrum model improved diagnostic consistency.
current_criteria_summary: Autism Spectrum Disorder is diagnosed based on persistent deficits in social communication/interaction plus restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, rated across three severity levels.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: PDD-NOS was folded into Autism Spectrum Disorder as a single unified diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Same rationale as Asperger's merge — spectrum model replaced separate subtypes.
current_criteria_summary: See Autism Spectrum Disorder criteria — spectrum-based severity rating replacing separate subtype labels.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: Eliminated as a separate diagnosis, absorbed into Autism Spectrum Disorder.
clinical_rationale: Consolidation of autism-related subtypes under one spectrum model.
current_criteria_summary: See Autism Spectrum Disorder criteria.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: All schizophrenia subtypes (paranoid, catatonic, disorganized, undifferentiated, residual) were removed; schizophrenia is now diagnosed as a single condition with symptom dimension ratings.
clinical_rationale: Subtypes showed poor reliability and limited treatment or prognostic value in longitudinal studies.
current_criteria_summary: Schizophrenia is diagnosed via core symptom criteria (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, etc.) rated on severity dimensions rather than subtype.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Schizophrenia Spectrum, 2013

change_summary: Catatonic subtype removed; catatonia is now a specifier that can apply across multiple diagnoses, not a schizophrenia subtype.
clinical_rationale: Catatonia occurs across many conditions, not just schizophrenia — reclassifying it as a specifier improved diagnostic accuracy.
current_criteria_summary: Catatonia specifier applied when relevant motor/behavioral symptoms are present.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Schizophrenia Spectrum, 2013

change_summary: The 'bereavement exclusion' was removed — grief no longer automatically rules out an MDD diagnosis if criteria are otherwise met.
clinical_rationale: Evidence showed grief-triggered depression can be clinically significant and undertreated if automatically excluded.
current_criteria_summary: MDD can be diagnosed even in the context of recent bereavement if full symptom criteria and duration are met, with clinical judgment distinguishing normal grief from disorder.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Depressive Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Substance Abuse and Substance Dependence were merged into a single Substance Use Disorder diagnosis with severity ratings (mild/moderate/severe).
clinical_rationale: The abuse/dependence split had weak empirical support; a single severity-graded disorder better reflected clinical presentation.
current_criteria_summary: Substance Use Disorder is diagnosed via 11 criteria with severity determined by symptom count (2-3=mild, 4-5=moderate, 6+=severe).
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Substance-Related Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Renamed from Gender Identity Disorder to Gender Dysphoria, shifting focus from identity as pathology to the distress caused by incongruence.
clinical_rationale: Reduces stigma by framing distress, not identity itself, as the clinical concern.
current_criteria_summary: Gender Dysphoria focuses on clinically significant distress related to incongruence between experienced and assigned gender.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Gender Dysphoria, 2013

change_summary: Terminology updated; diagnostic focus shifted to include adaptive functioning alongside IQ scores.
clinical_rationale: Reduces stigma; better reflects real-world functional impact beyond IQ score alone.
current_criteria_summary: Intellectual Disability diagnosed via deficits in intellectual functioning AND adaptive functioning across conceptual, social, and practical domains.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Intellectual Disability, 2013

new_label: Somatic Symptom Disorder / Illness Anxiety Disorder
change_summary: Hypochondriasis was split into two diagnoses depending on presence of somatic symptoms.
clinical_rationale: Better differentiates patients with predominant physical symptoms vs predominant health anxiety without significant symptoms.
current_criteria_summary: Somatic Symptom Disorder involves distressing physical symptoms with excessive thoughts/behaviors; Illness Anxiety Disorder involves high health anxiety with minimal/no somatic symptoms.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Somatic Symptom Disorders, 2013

change_summary: New diagnosis added specifically to address overdiagnosis of pediatric bipolar disorder in children with chronic irritability.
clinical_rationale: Addressed a documented pattern of children being misdiagnosed with bipolar disorder for chronic temper outbursts.
current_criteria_summary: DMDD is diagnosed in children with severe recurrent temper outbursts plus persistently irritable mood, distinct from episodic bipolar mood changes.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Depressive Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Elevated from an example under 'Eating Disorder NOS' in DSM-IV to a fully recognized standalone diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Recognized as a distinct, prevalent condition requiring its own diagnostic criteria and treatment approach.
current_criteria_summary: Binge Eating Disorder involves recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with loss of control, without regular compensatory behaviors, at defined frequency/duration thresholds.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Feeding and Eating Disorders, 2013

change_summary: ICD-11 introduced Complex PTSD as a distinct diagnosis from PTSD, capturing effects of prolonged, repeated trauma.
clinical_rationale: Clinical evidence showed prolonged/repeated trauma (e.g., childhood abuse) produces a distinguishable symptom pattern beyond standard PTSD criteria.
current_criteria_summary: Complex PTSD includes core PTSD symptoms plus disturbances in self-organization: emotional regulation difficulty, negative self-concept, and relationship difficulties.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

change_summary: Moved out of the 'Mental and Behavioural Disorders' chapter entirely into a new 'Conditions Related to Sexual Health' chapter.
clinical_rationale: Reflects evidence that gender incongruence itself is not a mental disorder, reducing stigma while retaining access to care coding.
current_criteria_summary: Gender Incongruence is classified under sexual health, not mental disorders, focused on marked incongruence between experienced gender and assigned sex.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

change_summary: New behavioral addiction diagnosis added to ICD-11, not present in ICD-10.
clinical_rationale: Growing clinical and research evidence of impaired control over gaming behavior causing significant functional impairment.
current_criteria_summary: Gaming Disorder involves impaired control over gaming, increasing priority over other activities, and continuation despite negative consequences, for at least 12 months.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

new_label: Bipolar Disorder with Mixed Features specifier
change_summary: The standalone 'Mixed Episode' category was removed; 'mixed features' is now a specifier that can be applied to manic, hypomanic, or depressive episodes.
clinical_rationale: Allowed more flexible and accurate description of patients showing overlapping manic and depressive symptoms rather than forcing a rigid separate category.
current_criteria_summary: Mixed features specifier applies when a manic, hypomanic, or major depressive episode includes at least three symptoms of the opposite pole.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Bipolar and Related Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Dysthymic Disorder and chronic Major Depressive Disorder were merged into a single diagnosis: Persistent Depressive Disorder.
clinical_rationale: Research did not support meaningful clinical distinction between chronic MDD and dysthymia; merging simplified diagnosis of chronic depressive presentations.
current_criteria_summary: Persistent Depressive Disorder is diagnosed when depressed mood persists for at least two years, with specifiers indicating severity and course.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Depressive Disorders, 2013

new_label: Reactive Attachment Disorder / Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder
change_summary: The single Reactive Attachment Disorder category was split into two distinct diagnoses based on differing symptom presentations.
clinical_rationale: Evidence showed the inhibited and disinhibited presentations of early attachment disruption have different courses and needed separate diagnostic criteria.
current_criteria_summary: RAD involves inhibited, emotionally withdrawn behavior toward caregivers; DSED involves indiscriminate, overly familiar behavior toward unfamiliar adults.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorders, 2013

new_label: Removed from DSM (diagnosed via genetic testing)
change_summary: Rett's Disorder was removed from the diagnostic manual entirely, as it is now understood to have a known genetic cause (MECP2 gene mutation) and is diagnosed medically, not psychiatrically.
clinical_rationale: Advances in genetic testing made a behavioral/psychiatric diagnostic category unnecessary and clinically inaccurate.
current_criteria_summary: No longer a psychiatric diagnosis; identified via genetic testing for MECP2 gene mutation.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: Pain Disorder was folded into the broader Somatic Symptom Disorder category rather than remaining a standalone diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Consolidation reflected evidence that pain-predominant somatic presentations did not warrant a separate diagnostic category from other somatic symptom presentations.
current_criteria_summary: Somatic Symptom Disorder involves one or more distressing somatic symptoms (which may include pain) with excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to the symptoms.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Somatic Symptom Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Moved out of Anxiety Disorders into its own chapter 'Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders'.
clinical_rationale: Recognized unique neurobiological and phenomenological features distinct from typical anxiety disorders.
current_criteria_summary: Diagnosis requires presence of obsessions, compulsions, or both, that are time-consuming or cause clinically significant distress.

change_summary: Moved out of Anxiety Disorders into a new 'Trauma and Stressor-Related Disorders' chapter.
clinical_rationale: Recognized that PTSD involves prominent anhedonic, dysphoric, and externalizing symptoms, not just anxiety.
current_criteria_summary: Exposure to trauma with intrusion, avoidance, negative alterations in cognitions/mood, and arousal/reactivity symptoms.

change_summary: Criteria expanded to require 9 of 14 symptoms from any category, rather than symptoms from specific clusters.
clinical_rationale: Improved diagnostic accuracy by recognizing that acute trauma reactions are highly variable across individuals.
current_criteria_summary: Diagnosis requires 9 or more symptoms from any of the five categories (intrusion, negative mood, dissociation, avoidance, arousal).

change_summary: Somatization Disorder was merged into Somatic Symptom Disorder, requiring distress/impairment rather than specific symptom counts.
clinical_rationale: The previous symptom counting was overly complex and unreliable; focus shifted to the distress caused by symptoms.
current_criteria_summary: One or more somatic symptoms causing distress/impairment, with excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to them.

change_summary: Renamed to Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder to better reflect clinical understanding and reduce stigma.
clinical_rationale: The term 'conversion' implied a specific psychoanalytic mechanism lacking empirical support in all cases.
current_criteria_summary: One or more symptoms of altered voluntary motor or sensory function with evidence of incompatibility with recognized neurological conditions.

change_summary: Dementia renamed to Major Neurocognitive Disorder.
clinical_rationale: Reduced stigma associated with the term 'dementia' and better encompasses conditions affecting younger individuals.
current_criteria_summary: Evidence of significant cognitive decline from a previous level of performance that interferes with independence in everyday activities.

change_summary: Formalized as Minor Neurocognitive Disorder for cognitive decline that doesn't significantly impair independence.
clinical_rationale: Allowed for earlier clinical identification and intervention for cognitive decline before it reaches the threshold of major impairment.
current_criteria_summary: Evidence of modest cognitive decline that does not interfere with capacity for independence in everyday activities.

change_summary: Added as a new standalone diagnosis, previously considered a subtype or symptom of OCD.
clinical_rationale: Evidence showed hoarding has distinct neurobiology, clinical presentation, and treatment response compared to OCD.
current_criteria_summary: Persistent difficulty discarding or parting with possessions, regardless of actual value, resulting in accumulation that congests living areas.

change_summary: Added as a new diagnosis under Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders.
clinical_rationale: Recognized as a distinct, prevalent condition causing significant distress and requiring specific treatment.
current_criteria_summary: Recurrent skin picking resulting in skin lesions, with repeated attempts to decrease or stop the behavior.

change_summary: Moved from Impulse Control Disorders to Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders.
clinical_rationale: Better aligns with conditions that share similar phenomenological features and treatment approaches.
current_criteria_summary: Recurrent pulling out of one's hair resulting in hair loss, with repeated attempts to decrease or stop the behavior.

change_summary: Age of onset criterion extended from before age 7 to before age 12.
clinical_rationale: Extensive research found no clinical difference between those with onset before 7 versus before 12, improving diagnosis for later-presenting cases.
current_criteria_summary: Persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity interfering with functioning, with several symptoms present prior to age 12.

change_summary: Replaced specific reading, math, and written expression disorders with a single overarching Specific Learning Disorder diagnosis with specifiers.
clinical_rationale: Simplified diagnosis as these deficits frequently co-occur and share underlying cognitive vulnerabilities.
current_criteria_summary: Difficulties learning and using academic skills persisting for at least 6 months despite provision of interventions.

change_summary: Added as a brand new diagnosis for persistent, impairing grief lasting longer than a year for adults (6 months for children).
clinical_rationale: Recognized that a subset of individuals experience severe, intractable grief requiring specific clinical intervention.
current_criteria_summary: Persistent and pervasive grief response characterized by intense longing or preoccupation with the deceased, lasting >12 months (adults).

change_summary: Reintroduced into the DSM-5-TR after being removed in DSM-5.
clinical_rationale: Restored to allow classification of mood presentations that do not meet full criteria for any specific bipolar or depressive disorder.
current_criteria_summary: Used when symptoms characteristic of a mood disorder cause distress but do not meet full criteria for any specific diagnostic class.

change_summary: Added as a new specific diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Acknowledges the potential cognitive impacts of chronic stimulant use.
current_criteria_summary: Mild neurocognitive impairment specifically attributed to the effects of stimulant use.

change_summary: Updated specifiers and support level descriptors for increased clarity.
clinical_rationale: Refined language to improve clinical utility and diagnostic precision without changing core criteria.
current_criteria_summary: Updated descriptors for 'requiring support', 'requiring substantial support', and 'requiring very substantial support'.

change_summary: Reclassified and updated conceptualization of fatigue syndromes.
clinical_rationale: Modernized terminology and criteria reflecting updated clinical consensus.
current_criteria_summary: Characterized by profound fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and unrefreshing sleep.

change_summary: Added as a new diagnosis under Impulse Control Disorders.
clinical_rationale: Recognized the clinical reality of persistent inability to control intense sexual impulses causing marked distress.
current_criteria_summary: Persistent pattern of failure to control intense sexual impulses or urges resulting in repetitive sexual behaviour over an extended period.

change_summary: Replaced the entire Somatoform Disorders block with Bodily Distress Disorder.
clinical_rationale: Shifted focus away from 'medically unexplained' to the presence of distressing bodily symptoms and disproportionate attention to them.
current_criteria_summary: Presence of bodily symptoms that are distressing to the individual, accompanied by excessive attention directed toward the symptoms.

change_summary: Completely restructured from categorical models (e.g., borderline, narcissistic) to a single dimensional model based on severity and trait domains.
clinical_rationale: Categorical models lacked validity and reliability; dimensional models better capture the spectrum of personality dysfunction.
current_criteria_summary: Diagnosed based on global severity of personality dysfunction (mild, moderate, severe) and five prominent trait domains (e.g., negative affectivity).

change_summary: Severity specifiers updated and simplified compared to ICD-10.
clinical_rationale: Improved global applicability and clinical utility of depressive episode severity ratings.
current_criteria_summary: Characterized by depressed mood or loss of interest, with severity determined by the number and intensity of symptoms and functional impairment.

change_summary: Redefined strictly as an occupational phenomenon, explicitly stating it is NOT classified as a medical condition.
clinical_rationale: Clarified that burnout is related specifically to workplace stress that has not been successfully managed.
current_criteria_summary: Syndrome conceptualized as resulting from chronic workplace stress, characterized by exhaustion, increased mental distance from job, and reduced professional efficacy.
